mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.2%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in accommodative monetary conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% (from a prior low) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is positive and industrial production (INDPRO) is declining (from the prior month), the economy shows signs of demand weakness despite production resilience, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in an imminent slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 > 19000 and INDPRO < 100.5.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 0.05%), the market anticipates reduced liquidity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index exceeding 270 (indicating accelerating inflation) triggers investor concerns about central bank rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 270.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1600 (thousands of units) reflect strong consumer demand for residential construction, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market prices in continued economic expansion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 1600.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth (PAYEMS > 140000) and unemployment rate decline (UNRATE < 5.5%) occur simultaneously, the labor market strengthens, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending increases.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 140000 and UNRATE < 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (INDPRO > 100.5), the supply chain faces inflationary pressures that lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates a potential recession.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO > 100.5.
